spec_match.rationale: Probes the exact CSS Overflow 3 §3.1 contract: clip preserved next to scrollable values (the change), visible→auto coercion (unchanged), and clip-axis immovability, via real getComputedStyle and scrollTop/scrollLeft assignments on a real scroller — no invented vocabulary.

interactive.rationale: Radio picker applies five real overflow pairs to a live scroller; script-attack buttons genuinely try to move each axis; readouts are computed from the DOM every time and the probe returns the coerced value (observed 'hidden' in Chromium 141 — it can fail).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index promises applying real pairs, reading back computed values, and script-scrolling the clipped axis; the page delivers exactly those three.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers scroll clip, the legacy scroll hidden contrast, scroll visible (unchanged coercion), clip clip (no scroll container), and auto clip; each option's verdict cell explains which rule fired.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5067363861004288 first, then the exact spec section and the explainer.

conformance.rationale: The suite's shorthand/longhand clip-preserved and clip-axis-rejects-programmatic-scroll assertions mirror exactly what this page probes; observed 5 pass / 3 fail (the three discriminators) on Chromium 141 — honest fails, no fake success.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 verified the legacy branch end-to-end (banner, coerced table verdict in rose, scrollTop=60 attack succeeding, clean console); the supported branch (clip preserved, axis refusing to move) could not be observed because no Chrome 152/Canary is available in this sandbox.

telemetry_health.rationale: sasc-probe-clip-preserved fires only when detection says supported; the coerced browser path reports the separate sasc-probe-legacy-coercion-fallback id, so a fallback is never counted as a pass.

design_system.rationale: All colours are CSS variables, verdict colours (accent-rose/emerald) sit on paper/ivory backgrounds at AA, and no button background is overridden.

accessibility.rationale: Native radios in a legended fieldset with 44px-min rows, native buttons, role=status aria-live=polite readout narrating every probe result in text, focus-visible outline on radio labels, and the stage is keyboard-focusable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×1600: scrollWidth equals viewport on both (no horizontal overflow), the two-panel grid stacks under 720px, the readout table scrolls in its own container, tap targets ≥44px; console clean apart from the environmental fonts.googleapis failure.

openQuestions.title: Capture the supported-branch evidence on Chrome 152 or flagged Canary
openQuestions.detail: Run the page in Chrome 152+ (or 150/151 with --enable-blink-features=SingleAxisScrollContainers) and confirm the emerald 'clip preserved — single-axis' verdict, the scrollTop attack refusing to move, and the sasc-probe-clip-preserved telemetry id firing; then refresh this critique's runtime_evidence to pass.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: overflow: clip prevents all scrolling (user and programmatic), unlike hidden which remains script-scrollable; use clip for true no-scroll clipping.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: This distinction is the page's core teaching: the script-attack buttons demonstrate hidden moving under script while a genuine clip axis refuses, and the copy states the contract in the same terms.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel radio group fieldset live region status readout no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use minmax(0,1fr) grid tracks and per-container overflow so wide content never forces page-level horizontal scroll.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The two-panel layout uses grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr) collapsing to one column at 720px, and the computed-value table sits in an overflow-x:auto wrapper; measured scrollWidth == innerWidth on both classes.

summary: The honest single-probe page for the feature: it applies real overflow pairs, reads back the browser's actual computed values, and attacks both axes with script. On sandbox Chromium 141 it correctly reports the legacy clip→hidden coercion in an amber banner with exact flag steps; nothing is simulated, and the pass telemetry only fires when the computed value is genuinely clip.
